simple.meaning: שָׁתַם (shâtham) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to unveil (figuratively).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Numbers, beginning at Numbers 24:3. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁתַם (H8365) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שָׁתַם (shâtham) / H8365 is traced through Numbers 24:3, Numbers 24:15 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H8365. shatham [ שָׁתַם ] verb dubious; if text correct, open (Late Hebrew Aramaic שׁתם open [vessel]); — only Qal Passive participle construct הְעָ֑יִן שְׁתֻם הַגֶּבֶר Num 24:3 , 15 (poems in J E) the man opened of [mental] eye , so ᵑ6 Ki Ew and others RVm; ᵑ9 Rö Ke Di and others render closed of [bodily] eye , reading then implicity שְׂתֻם (compare שָׂתַם סָתַם, Lam 3:8 ); see further Gray. [ הִשְׁתִּין שׁתן, ] see שִׁין .
